before.positive:
A real photograph, a still frame from a live-action commercial shot on a large-format 65mm digital cinema camera. EXACTLY 2 people in frame: Priya on the left, Tom on the right.

Priya: left of frame, about 1.5 metres from camera. Tom: right of frame, about 1.6 metres from camera. Priya and Tom hug each other, every hand resting on the other's back and traceable to a shoulder. Every grey figure in the layout is a real person and every grey shape is a real object: the pavement, the road, cars, buildings, trees.

Camera at about 1.7 metres above the ground, looking slightly down, 30mm lens, natural perspective, background slightly soft.

Priya is the one in image 3: a woman in her 20s with a long dark braid, light blue denim jacket over a white t-shirt, black jeans. Tom is the one in image 4: a man in his 20s with short blond hair, olive green bomber jacket, khaki chinos, white sneakers.

Cracked asphalt with faded lane paint, scuffed concrete kerbs and pavement, weathered building walls with stains and patched render, painted metal bodywork with reflections and road dust on the lower panels, weathered concrete, real trees with rough bark.

Late-afternoon sun from camera left, about 30 degrees high. The light falls directly on the subjects and the ground around them. Exposed for the main subject; shadows stay open, with readable texture in the ground and foreground, never pure black.

Tactile realism: readable colour, soft highlight roll-off, truthful skin colour, restrained fine grain over a sharp image. Texture comes from real surfaces and light, never a filter. Any signs or screens have no readable letters.

If any surface looks clean, plastic, grey, untextured or rendered, the image is wrong.
